Two unlimited baskets allow at most two distinct types inside the window. The frequency map records how many copies of each type remain, rather than merely whether that type was ever observed. On adding a third type, move left until an entire old type leaves the window. Partial removals of a repeated type do not release its basket.

concept.question: Why does a third fruit type force the starting tree to move?

concept.observation: Basket capacity limits distinct types, not total fruit count.
approach: Count types in the current continuous section.
Expand right, shrinking left only when a third type appears.

concept.correctness: For each right endpoint, shrinking removes only starts whose section still has more than two types. Removing left values cannot add a type, so the first retained start gives the longest valid section ending there. A discarded start cannot regain validity by adding later trees. Maximizing those endpoint results finds the best continuous harvest.

complexity.explanation: Every tree enters and leaves the section at most once. The count map holds at most three types during adjustment, giving linear time and constant extra storage.

pitfalls: Basket capacity limits distinct types, not total fruit count.
